newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HudCon wants Packer to sell Crown shares.
newsitem.headline: HudCon wants Packer to sell Crown shares.

text.p: Hudson Conway Ltd chief executive Lloyd Williams called on Australian's richest man Kerry Packer on Thursday to sell the remaining 50 million shares he owns in the Melbourne casino operator Crown Casino Ltd.
"I think he (Packer) is probably the cause for the share price to be languishing a bit...", Williams told reporters after a meeting of shareholders.

"It would have been better in my view if he had sold the balance of 50 million shares he still owns. The market perceives that as an overhang of the stock. So that is not an advantage," Williams said.

"I would like to encourage him to sell that last 50 million," he said. Packer's Consolidated Press holdings Ltd sold 75 million Crown shares in September and said it would not sell its remaining stake for at least six months.
Packer owns about 20 percent of Hudson Conway, which in turn is the largest shareholder in Crown, the Melbourne casino operator, with a 37 percent stake.
Packer also owns a 45 percent stake in media group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
At 10.10 a.m. (2310 GMT), Crown shares were already at A$2.75. Its shares have fallen from its 1996 high of A$3.06, hit on September 6, which was a few weeks before Packer reduced his stake.
